display.purpose: The report title in the masthead. Serif, the only fluid (clamp) step.

headline.purpose: File name headings, prefixed by a small mono file-index counter.

body.purpose: Commentary prose and summary values. Serif, held to the 38ch margin measure.

code.purpose: Diff lines. Mono, the primary text of the body column.

label.purpose: Card-type labels, file tags, summary keys. Mono, short, never all-caps sentences.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Note state changes: background, border, ring, and the range chip recolor.

motion.name: highlight
motion.purpose: Diff-line background transition when an annotated range is highlighted.

motion.name: scroll
motion.purpose: scroll-behavior when a note scrolls its first line into view; falls back to auto under reduced-motion.

components.name: Commentary Note
components.description: The signature margin note. Serif body, a mono type-label with a leading dot in the type's hue, and a quiet right-aligned range chip naming the lines it explains. Clickable to reveal those lines.
components.html:
observationL2–4

The whole association block changes here, not just one line; the chip names the range.
components.css: .ds-note { font-family: 'Iowan Old Style', Palatino, Georgia, serif; position: relative; border: 1px solid oklch(89% 0.006 250); border-radius: 9px; background: oklch(97.2% 0.005 250); padding: 12px 15px; font-size: 0.93rem; line-height: 1.65; color: oklch(30% 0.02 255); max-width: 38ch; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.16s ease, border-color 0.16s ease, box-shadow 0.16s ease; } .ds-note p { margin: 0; } .ds-note__label { font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.02em; margin-bottom: 6px; display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 7px; color: oklch(48% 0.13 250); } .ds-note__label::before { content: ''; flex: 0 0 auto; width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-note__range { margin-left: auto; flex: 0 0 auto; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.68rem; letter-spacing: 0.01em; color: oklch(52% 0.015 255); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-note--concept .ds-note__label { color: oklch(46% 0.16 300); } .ds-note--warn .ds-note__label { color: oklch(48% 0.10 70); } .ds-note--surprise .ds-note__label { color: oklch(50% 0.18 25); } .ds-note:hover { background: oklch(95.5% 0.006 250); border-color: oklch(83% 0.008 250); } .ds-note:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid oklch(56% 0.11 215); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Commentary Note (active)
components.description: The selected note. The one moment color asserts itself: accent-tint wash, teal border, 1px teal ring (a crisp outline, never a soft shadow), and the range chip recolored to accent-ink.
components.html:
conceptL5–7

Selecting the note reveals exactly these lines in the diff; nothing is drawn at rest.

components.name: Diff Body
components.description: The body column: mono code lines on a cool code-surface, with a docked mono file header. Add/remove pair tint with a +/- glyph; highlighted lines deepen and gain an inset accent bar.

components.css: .ds-diff { font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; max-width: 640px; } .ds-diff__header { font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 600; color: oklch(46% 0.02 255); background: oklch(97.2% 0.005 250); border: 1px solid oklch(89% 0.006 250); border-bottom: none; border-radius: 8px 8px 0 0; padding: 9px 14px; } .ds-diff__body { margin: 0; font-size: 0.8rem; line-height: 1.6; display: flex; flex-direction: column; border: 1px solid oklch(89% 0.006 250); border-radius: 0 0 8px 8px; background: oklch(97.8% 0.005 248); overflow-x: auto; } .ds-dl { display: block; white-space: pre; padding: 0 16px 0 6px; color: oklch(46% 0.02 255); } .ds-dl--add { background: oklch(95% 0.05 150); color: oklch(30% 0.02 255); } .ds-dl--rm { background: oklch(95.5% 0.05 25); color: oklch(30% 0.02 255); } .ds-dl--hunk { background: oklch(96.5% 0.02 215); color: oklch(40% 0.10 218); font-style: italic; } .ds-dl--hi { box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 oklch(56% 0.11 215); } .ds-dl--add.ds-dl--hi { background: oklch(92.5% 0.075 150); } .ds-dl--rm.ds-dl--hi { background: oklch(93% 0.075 25); }

components.name: Summary Block
components.description: The masthead abstract: a definition list with mono uppercase keys and serif values, plus an italic interaction hint divided off by a hairline.
components.html:
What
Folds adjacent diff hunks so one note can span a logical change.
Why
The raw diff splits a single refactor across hunks; readers think in changes, not hunks.

Select a note to trace it to its lines.
components.css: .ds-summary { font-family: 'Iowan Old Style', Palatino, Georgia, serif; border: 1px solid oklch(89% 0.006 250); border-radius: 10px; background: oklch(97.2% 0.005 250); padding: 18px 22px; max-width: 72ch; color: oklch(30% 0.02 255); line-height: 1.65; } .ds-summary dl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; gap: 4px 14px; margin: 0; } .ds-summary dt { font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.7rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: oklch(52% 0.015 255); padding-top: 0.35em; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-summary dd { margin: 0; color: oklch(30% 0.02 255); } .ds-summary__hint { grid-column: 1 / -1; margin: 10px 0 0; padding-top: 10px; border-top: 1px solid oklch(89% 0.006 250); font-size: 0.85rem; color: oklch(46% 0.02 255); font-style: italic; }

narrative.overview: The report reads like a scholar's annotated edition of a manuscript: a literate-programming document where prose and code are equal citizens on the page. Commentary lives in the margin like a knowledgeable colleague's notes; the diff sits in the body as the primary text. Each note names the lines it explains with a quiet mono range chip, and selecting the note reveals those exact lines in the body with an accent highlight, one note at a time, so the diff stays clean at rest. The reader is usually landing in an unfamiliar codebase, so the surface has one job before any other: be calm and legible. This is a light, paper-like surface, not a dark IDE. The body is a cool near-white paper, deliberately not the warm cream/sand AI default, and color is restrained and strictly semantic. Type does the heavy lifting: an editorial serif for prose against a mono for code gives an instant read of 'this is explanation' vs. 'this is the change.' Saturated color appears only where it carries meaning: a diff tint, a card type, a file tag, or the single calm teal that marks the active note.
keyCharacteristics: Light, cool paper reading surface; ink-on-paper calm, never a dark IDE.
Restrained palette: color is reserved for functional meaning, never decoration.
Serif prose beside mono code, type rather than chrome carries the hierarchy.
Two-column margin-and-body layout; the note→line link is the signature interaction, revealed on demand rather than always drawn.
Color-blind safe by construction: every encoding pairs hue with a label, glyph, or position.

rules.name: The Quiet Surface Rule
rules.body: The paper and ink carry the page. Saturated color appears only where it encodes meaning: a diff line, a card type, a file tag, or the active link. If a color isn't carrying information, it doesn't belong on the surface.

rules.name: The No-Hue-Only Rule
rules.body: Every color-coded distinction is reinforced by a non-color cue: diff lines pair tint with a +/- glyph; card types pair hue with a written label and a leading dot; file tags pair hue with the tag word and a currentColor border; the active highlight pairs the teal tint with a positional inset marker on the line. The report must read fully in grayscale and to color-blind readers.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Exactly one accent hue (teal, hue 215) means 'active.' It is kept off the entire semantic wheel (diff hues, card hues, tag hues) so the eye never confuses 'selected' with 'this is an addition' or 'this is a concept note.'

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Serif speaks for the human (commentary, headings); mono speaks for the machine (code, tags, labels). Never blur them: prose is never set in mono, code is never set in serif. This is the system's primary hierarchy mechanism, replacing the borders and chrome a diff tool would use.

rules.name: The Flat-Paper Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows on notes, panels, or tags. Separation comes from hairline rules, generous whitespace, and a faint tonal shift between margin and body.

rules.name: The Ring-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: The single 'lift' in the system, the active note, is expressed as a teal border plus a 1px ring of the same color, i.e. a crisp outline, never a soft blurred shadow. State asserts itself through color and a hairline ring, not through faked depth.

dos: Do keep the surface light and cool-paper; let ink and serif type carry the page.
Do reserve saturated color for functional meaning only (The Quiet Surface Rule).
Do pair every color-coded distinction with a label, glyph, dot, or position (The No-Hue-Only Rule); the report must read in grayscale and for color-blind readers.
Do set commentary in serif and code in mono, always (The Two-Voice Rule).
Do keep one teal as the only 'active' hue, off the entire semantic wheel (The One Teal Rule).
Do separate surfaces with hairlines and tonal shifts, never drop shadows (The Flat-Paper Rule).
Do keep commentary prose at the 38ch margin measure and hit at least 4.5:1 contrast for all body text.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion alternative (kill smooth scroll and transitions) and full keyboard operation for the note-to-line interaction.
donts: Don't make it look like GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket diff chrome — no #0d1117 dark clone, no platform-diff styling the reader already knows.
Don't use generic AI/SaaS styling: no purple gradients, glassmorphism, hero-metric cards, or tiny tracked uppercase eyebrows.
Don't add noisy IDE chrome — no line-number gutters, minimaps, toolbars, or panel stacks. This is for reading, not editing.
Don't let it feel cold, corporate, or like a compliance PDF — it should read as deliberately made and human.
Don't use a border-left greater than 1px as a colored type stripe on notes (the banned side-stripe pattern); encode card type with the label + dot instead.
Don't default the body background to warm cream/sand/parchment (the saturated AI neutral); keep paper cool and at minimal, intentional chroma.
Don't set body prose in a light 'elegant' gray; bump toward ink until contrast is comfortable.
Don't let 'active' teal collide with any semantic hue; if selection looks like an add or a concept note, the accent has drifted onto the wheel.
